narrative: Fire and climate dominate today's batch: modelling work projects European burned area could rise by roughly 39% under a low-emission pathway as fire weather intensifies, while remote sensing reveals post-fire vegetation shifts becoming visible across Siberian boreal forest. Several studies document climate-driven behavioural and phenological change — warming is breaking down plant-pollinator mutualisms despite maintained phenological synchrony, drought reshapes elephant space use across timescales, and shifting space use is creating camouflage mismatches that raise extinction risk in an endangered squirrel. Trophic and symbiotic interactions feature strongly: a new superposition method offers a faster route to reconstructing food-web trophic positions, mycorrhizal complementarity is shown to strengthen diversity-productivity relationships in tree communities, and goose grazing restructures microbial nutrient-cycling potential in a sub-Arctic wetland. On the applied side, conservation and landscape papers evaluate riparian buffer effectiveness, canopy interventions for bat conservation, and safe limits on clearcut accumulation for boreal forest birds, alongside a global synthesis comparing the effectiveness of current versus potential conservation actions for amphibians, birds and mammals. In invasion ecology, niche reorganisation in crayfish invasions and native-patch-size effects on grassland invasion resistance both point to spatial and structural drivers of establishment success. Methods contributions include a zero-shot bioacoustic classifier for anuran calls trained across continents and a Bayesian dynamic mixing model bridging static and dynamic approaches to isotopic diet estimation.
